title: Where the optimum can be

blocks.text: The warehouse-siting search prints a progress line after every node, so the planners can see how close it is to done. Each line needs the range the optimum must lie in.

Write `optimum_range(incumbent, waiting, tol=1e-6)` in `optimum_range.py`. `incumbent` is the best plan's value so far (`None` before the first plan); `waiting` is the list of bounds carried by the nodes still waiting to be solved (each one its parent's LP value). Return `(low, high, proven)`:
With no incumbent, `low` is `None`, `high` is the largest waiting bound, and `proven` is `False`. With no incumbent and nothing waiting, return `(None, None, False)`. The problem is a maximization.

from __future__ import annotations


def optimum_range(incumbent: float | None, waiting: list[float], tol: float = 1e-6):
    """(low, high, proven): the optimum lies in [low, high]; proven when the two ends meet."""
    candidates = list(waiting)
    if incumbent is not None:
        candidates.append(incumbent)
    high = max(candidates) if candidates else None
    if incumbent is None:
        return None, high, False
    return incumbent, high, high - incumbent <= tol


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(optimum_range(None, [812.5]))
    print(optimum_range(780.0, [812.5, 790.25]))
    print(optimum_range(805.0, [800.0]))

    """(low, high, proven): the optimum lies in [low, high]; proven when the two ends meet."""
